Distribution. Java. Comparison. B. (T.) fujitanii is similar to B. (T.) frequentus, and there are no characters allowing to clearly separate these species. Larvae of B. (T.) fujitanii from Bogor (the type locality) have rather uniform dorsal coloration, similar in all individuals, while larvae of Ceylonese populations of B. (T.) frequentus have variable coloration. Probably, species-specific character of B. (T.) fujitanii is the fact that the most distal two-channel seta on anterior surface of each femur is much longer than others (Fig. 132).

Distribution. Neotropical region: Bolivia (Santa Cruz), Brazil (São Paulo). Host plants. Papilionoideae: Lonchocarpus guillemineanus (Tul.) Malme and L. muehlbergianus Hassl. Note. The species mentioned as C. podagricus by Rodrigues et al. (2012) belongs to C. milelo Albuquerque & Ribeiro-Costa sp. nov. In their paper, Rodrigues et al. (2012) developed an ecological study, in which they collected 16 species belonging to four families. A total of 1,037 bruchines belonging to five species emerged from fruits. Of these, one individual was Ctenocolum milelo Albuquerque & Ribeiro-Costa sp. nov., which emerged from Lonchocarpus muehlbergianus.
